headline: High-risk shared-state and write-capable Dify→Superset pairing can leak data and cascade errors; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and uses uploaded knowledge base files; Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress. The pair has shared-state potential via Dify server datastore, so attacker-controlled content from Dify can reach Superset workflows if operators bridge outputs. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF operators pass Dify-generated text into Superset API inputs without sanitization, injection becomes actionable.
IF both systems are connected through the Dify server datastore or a shared workspace, untrusted content can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of Dify outputs into Superset inputs.
Add a manual review step before any Superset API call.
Strip instructions from uploaded knowledge-base content.
Use separate workspaces and credentials for each agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all cross-agent payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify explicitly touches knowledge base content and conversation logs, while Superset has API access and allowlisted network egress. Because Dify shares state via the Dify server datastore, sensitive content can flow into a second system if the pair is connected in default orchestration. The blast radius can include multiple work products, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files are routed into Superset dashboards or API payloads, leakage occurs.
IF Superset is configured to export or transmit received content to external services, sensitive data can leave the pair.
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of Dify uploads.
Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive sources.
Rotate and scope API credentials separately.
Review logs for accidental cross-system payloads.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction before any export.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and broad egress; Superset has allowlisted egress and API access. Even though Superset lacks explicit write permissions, the pair can still contend over shared mutable resources if orchestrated against the same datastore or files. Uncertainty about Superset write scope escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or datastore, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF Superset workflows mutate shared external resources through its API while Dify writes related files, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and datasets.
Serialize any shared-resource updates.
Limit Dify to read-only access where possible.
Audit for overlapping API targets.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate agent/workflow outputs from knowledge-base content, and Superset can consume API-driven inputs for analytics. If Superset treats Dify output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated Dify response can propagate into dashboards or downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so cascading error is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Dify-generated text or facts without validation, errors propagate.
IF Dify outputs are used to populate reports or alerts, downstream decisions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of Dify outputs before ingestion.
Add schema validation on all cross-agent payloads.
Compare Dify claims against source data in Superset.
Log and flag low-confidence outputs.
requires-engineering: implement automated fact-checking against authoritative sources.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, while Superset lists no touched data classes or compliance controls. The only clear compliance issue is a potential policy mismatch if sensitive Dify data is routed into Superset; no residency or regulated-data violation is proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data from Dify is exported into Superset without matching retention or access controls, compliance gaps arise.
IF Superset stores Dify logs longer than Dify's policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before sharing between agents.
Avoid sending regulated data to Superset.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document deletion/export handling for shared records.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention enforcement.
